H0: No linear relationship between alcohol and quality
Conclusion: Moderate positive linear relationship (r = 0.44): higher alcohol goes with higher quality.

H0: No monotonic relationship between alcohol and quality
Conclusion: Moderate positive monotonic relationship (rho = 0.44); confirms the Pearson result.

H0: Mean alcohol is equal in Good and Not Good wines
H1: Mean alcohol differs between the groups
Conclusion: Good wines have clearly higher mean alcohol (11.42 vs 10.27); Cohen's d = 1.01 (large effect).

H0: Alcohol has the same distribution in Good and Not Good wines
Conclusion: Distributions differ significantly; confirms the t-test without assuming normality.
Alcohol is not normally distributed, so rank-based tests (Spearman, Mann-Whitney) are a sensible check.
